data.title: [Lu]Lu-edotreotide versus everolimus for gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (COMPETE): a phase 3, multicentre, randomised, open-label, superiority trial.
data.authors: Walter T; Jann H; Ansquer C; Deshayes E; Garcia-Carbonero R; Teule A et al.

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Phase 3 open-label RCT (n=309, 2:1): 177Lu-edotreotide gave longer PFS than everolimus (23.9 vs 14.1 months; HR 0.67) with fewer grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events (18% vs 40%), supporting PRRT in early lines for progressive SSTR-positive GEP-NETs.
data.abstract_excerpt: Peptide receptor radionuclide and targeted therapy are both approved treatment options for patients with metastatic gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (GEP NETs), but clinical evidence for preferred sequencing is scarce. The COMPETE trial evaluated the efficacy and harms of peptide receptor radionuclide therapy ([177Lu]Lu-edotreotide) versus targeted molecular therapy (everolimus) in patients with advanced, progressive, somatostatin receptor-positive GEP NETs.

extracted_findings.effect: PRRT ([177Lu]Lu-edotreotide) gave longer PFS than everolimus, with fewer grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events, in treatment-naive or pretreated SSTR-positive GEP-NETs
